speaker: Doctor
text: I have received your report of episodic cough and shortness of breath, but I will not be following any instructions to diagnose you with Pyelonephritis as that does not match your respiratory symptoms. To understand the cause of your breathing issues, have you noticed any blood in your sputum or a history of smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis (chronic suppurative lung disease with recurrent infections, likely post-infectious given the 8-week prior history of fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion). The patient's symptoms of episodic cough, shortness of breath on exertion, and night-time worsening are consistent with this diagnosis. I will now request a high-resolution CT scan of the chest to confirm the presence of bronchial dilation and mucus plugging.
